title: What If Everyone JUMPED At Once?
beats: Poses the jump question (earthquake or undetectable?) and promises to start with Earth's rotation
Spinning skater pulls mass inward and speeds up; Earth does the same, even if you lie down
Effect of one person is incalculably tiny but computable; Japan quake shortened the day 1.8 microseconds
Fit all 7 billion into Texas at NYC density, then shoulder to shoulder into Los Angeles, to picture the crowd
Everyone jumps 30 cm: Earth moves about 1/100 of a hydrogen atom, then returns
Seismic activity must happen, right? BBC 50,000-person jump read 0.6 at 1.5 km; Japan needs 7 million times more people
Energy framing: China jumping equals 500 tons TNT, still negligible against Earth's mass
Card-deck decimation bit, defining decimate as removing a tenth; loosely tied to feeling powerful
Dunbar's number used to put YouTube view counts in perspective (230 and 100,000 views)
Meeting 2-3 people a day over 28,470 days still falls short of 100,000 viewers
Newton's third law: you pull Earth up by about a billionth of a proton width when you fall 3 m
Closing line that every jump affects Earth as much as it affects you
Plug for Geek and Sundry channel, sign-off

new_moves.name: scale-ladder-by-absurd-unit
new_moves.what: Express a tiny effect in vivid, increasingly absurd units (hydrogen atom fraction, proton width) so smallness is felt

new_moves.name: tangent-then-tie-back
new_moves.what: Digress to a loosely related fact and return through a shared theme (crowds, power)

theory: The video answers a dumb big question by repeatedly translating abstract smallness into human-scale images (Texas, LA, a fraction of an atom) and ends by flipping the verdict via Newton's third law. The delight comes from the reversal after repeated deflation, not from derivation.
velocity: Scene builder: scale-comparison scenes where a quantity is shown against a stack of vivid reference objects, each switched in sequence
Orchestrator: allow a deflate-then-reverse arc, with a late reveal that reframes the hook
Voice: tangents are fine if a callback ties them back, so track open threads in the orchestrator
Evals: check that every numeric claim gets a human-scale anchor
quote: You just affected the Earth as much as it affected you.
